review_notes: I read the whole file. I compared its simp lemmas with Mathlib's Teichmuller.lean (mk_teichmuller₀ and the teichmuller₀ normal-form lemmas), Perfection.lean (the @[simps] lift) and Perfect.lean. I also checked that RingHom.toMonoidWithZeroHom_eq_coe is not simp, so comp_teichmullerSection has a usable LHS. Other simp lemmas looked fine: coeff_lift (rfl, no loop), teichmullerSection_reduction_apply and comp_teichmullerSection. The two *_apply lemmas rewrite the ring-hom form to the multiplicative form, and that direction terminates. The only defect I found is the pair of shadowed simp lemmas below, and I did not run Lean, so it rests on how simp visits subterms (arguments are simplified before the enclosing application). The test file and FrobeniusCore do not rely on the redundant lemmas. The Perfection.coeff_lift RHS keeps an iterate of the inverse Frobenius, which is a reasonable normal form. I did not check whether it overlaps the simps-generated lemmas on Mathlib's Perfection.lift, because no lift_apply lemma appears in Mathlib's usages.

findings.excerpt:
theorem teichmullerSectionRingHom_reduction_apply (a : κ) :
    f (teichmullerSectionRingHom p f hf a) = a :=
findings.problem: This @[simp] lemma is shadowed by `teichmullerSectionRingHom_apply`, which is also @[simp] and is stated by `rfl`. Simp rewrites the inner term `teichmullerSectionRingHom p f hf a` to `teichmullerSection p f hf a` first. The outer `f (…)` then matches `teichmullerSection_reduction_apply`, so this lemma's LHS will normally never be seen. It adds a second simp rule for the same fact and enlarges the simp set without changing any simp result.
findings.proposed_change: Remove the `@[simp]` attribute from `teichmullerSectionRingHom_reduction_apply` and keep it as an ordinary lemma if wanted. `teichmullerSectionRingHom_apply` followed by `teichmullerSection_reduction_apply` is then the single canonical simp path.
findings.benefit: The simp set has one rule per normal form (the multiplicative section), with no overlapping lemma the simplifier cannot reach. A reader can see that the normal form of the ring-hom section is the `→*₀` section.

evidence.excerpt: teichmullerSectionRingHom p f hf a = teichmullerSection p f hf a := rfl
f (teichmullerSection p f hf a) = a

findings.excerpt:
theorem mk_teichmullerRingHom [CharP R p] (x : Perfection (R ⧸ I) p) :
    Ideal.Quotient.mk I (teichmullerRingHom p I x) = coeff _ p 0 x :=
  mk_teichmuller₀ x
findings.problem: This @[simp] lemma duplicates the composite of two existing simp rules. `teichmullerRingHom_apply` (simp, rfl) turns `teichmullerRingHom p I x` into `teichmuller₀ p I x`. Mathlib's simp lemma `mk_teichmuller₀` then gives `coeff _ p 0 x`. Its proof is literally `mk_teichmuller₀ x`. Because the inner term is rewritten first, the LHS shape `mk I (teichmullerRingHom p I x)` will not be reached by simp. This is a redundant, shadowed simp rule.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `mk_teichmullerRingHom`, or delete the lemma, since it is `mk_teichmuller₀` after unfolding `teichmullerRingHom_apply`. Keep only `teichmullerRingHom_apply` as the simp bridge to Mathlib's `teichmuller₀` normal form.
findings.benefit: Simp reasoning about the ring-hom Teichmüller map reduces to Mathlib's `teichmuller₀` lemmas through one bridge lemma. The file adds no parallel lemmas for the same facts, which keeps the simp set small and predictable.
